title: Vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all open coverings implies vanishing cohomology on every open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal F|_U$ be the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal F|_U)(W)=\mathcal F(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and $H^p(U,-)$ the cohomology of the scheme $U$ (an open subscheme of $X$), the right derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\mathcal O_U$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and a family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of opens with $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ be the corresponding covering of the Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$, where $X_{\rm Zar}$ is the site of open subschemes of $X$ with inclusions as morphisms and jointly surjective open families as coverings [def-sc-zariski-site]; in it the fibre product $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$ of opens $U_{i_k}\subseteq U$ is the intersection $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ with its inclusions (the category is a preordered set, so this is the only choice), and the projection omitting the $j$-th factor is the inclusion $U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}\subseteq U_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}$, and let $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ be the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups $W\mapsto\mathcal F(W)$ of $\mathcal F$ on $X_{\rm Zar}$ for $\mathcal U$ (degree $p$ term $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}\mathcal F(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$, alternating sum of restrictions as differential). Assume $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p>0$, every open $U\subseteq X$ and every such covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$. Then $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every open $U\subseteq X$. (Stacks states this for ringed spaces, with $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ the derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, which equal $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)$ by Lemma 01E1 (2).)

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish, line 1631) and its proof (embedding into an injective, Lemma 01EP lemma-injective-trivial-cech, Lemma 01EU lemma-ses-cech-h1, Lemma 01EK lemma-cech-cohomology-delta-functor-presheaves, Derived Categories Lemma 015B, dimension shifting); Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 496) (2) for H^p(U,F) = H^p(U,F|_U)

proof.text: **Step 1 (the induction).** Call an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ *Cech-acyclic* if $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $p>0$, every open $U\subseteq X$ and every open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $U$ (in the sense of the statement), i.e. if $\mathcal G$ satisfies the hypothesis of the lemma. For $p\ge1$ let $P(p)$ be the assertion: for every Cech-acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ and every open $U\subseteq X$, $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$. We prove $P(p)$ for all $p\ge1$ by induction on $p$, quantified over all Cech-acyclic $\mathcal G$ at once (Steps 2-8 for a fixed $\mathcal G$, Step 9 the induction); the lemma is $P(p)$ for $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$, which is Cech-acyclic by hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, ("We will indicate this by saying F has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any open covering"; "Since F was an arbitrary O_X-module with vanishing higher Cech cohomology ... And so on and so forth")

proof.text: **Step 2 (embedding into an injective).** Let $\mathcal G$ be Cech-acyclic. Since $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], choose a monomorphism $\iota:\mathcal G\to\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I$ an injective object of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\pi:\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal G$ be its cokernel in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $0\to\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal I\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (in an abelian category a monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel, and a cokernel is an epimorphism).

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an embedding F -> I into an injective O_X-module ... Let Q = I/F so that we have a short exact sequence")

proof.text: **Step 3 ($\mathcal I$ is Cech-acyclic).** By [lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic] (Stacks 01EP), applied to the injective $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal I$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$, every open $U\subseteq X$ and every open covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$.

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, ("By Lemma 01EP I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any open covering")

proof.text: **Step 4 (the sequence is exact on sections over every open).** Let $W\subseteq X$ be open. The sequence $0\to\mathcal G(W)\xrightarrow{\iota_W}\mathcal I(W)\xrightarrow{\pi_W}\mathcal Q(W)\to0$ of abelian groups is exact. Exactness at $\mathcal G(W)$ and $\mathcal I(W)$: by Step 2, $\iota$ is a kernel of $\pi$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ ($\iota$ is a monomorphism with image $\operatorname{Ker}\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]), and kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\iota_W$ is injective with image $\ker\pi_W$. Surjectivity of $\pi_W$: let $\Sigma$ be the set of all open coverings of $W$; it is cofinal (every open covering refines itself), and $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\Sigma$ because $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic; so [lem-weil-pbc-module-ses-cech-h1-surjective] (Stacks 01EU), applied to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$, the open $W$ and $\Sigma$, gives that $\pi_W:\mathcal I(W)\to\mathcal Q(W)$ is surjective. Thus $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is exact as a sequence of presheaves.

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, ("By Lemma 01EU and our assumptions this sequence is actually exact as a sequence of presheaves!")

proof.text: **Step 5 (short exact sequence of Cech complexes).** Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ an open covering of $U$, a covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site] whose fibre products are the intersections $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}$. The morphisms $\iota,\pi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are in particular morphisms of the underlying presheaves of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$, so they induce morphisms of Cech complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)$ (functoriality, part (e) of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]), with composite $0$. In degree $p\ge0$ this sequence is the product over $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}$ of the sequences $0\to\mathcal G(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})\to\mathcal I(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})\to\mathcal Q(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})\to0$, each short exact by Step 4 (with $W=U_{i_0\ldots i_p}$), and a product of short exact sequences of abelian groups is short exact (kernel and image of a product of homomorphisms are the products of the kernels and images); in degrees $p<0$ all terms are $0$. Hence $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of abelian groups, short exactness of complexes being degreewise [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact]. (This is the exactness of the Cech complex functor on presheaves that underlies Stacks 01EK.)

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, ("In particular we have a long exact sequence of Cech cohomology groups for any open covering U, see Lemma 01EK")

proof.text: **Step 6 ($\mathcal Q$ is Cech-acyclic).** For every open $U$ and open covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$, the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] of the short exact sequence of complexes of Step 5 contains, for each $p\ge1$, the exact piece $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^p}\check H^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. The left term is $0$ by Step 3 and the right term is $0$ because $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic and $p+1>0$; so $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)=0$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is again a Cech-acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, ("This implies that Q is also an O_X-module with vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all open coverings")

proof.text: **Step 7 (restriction to $U$).** Let $U\subseteq X$ be open. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives] (1), restriction $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A|_U$, $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, is additive and exact; applied to the short exact sequence of Step 2 (exact at each of its three middle positions, the zero objects going to zero objects since the functor is additive) it gives a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G|_U\xrightarrow{\iota|_U}\mathcal I|_U\xrightarrow{\pi|_U}\mathcal Q|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. By part (2) of the same lemma, $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module. Moreover $\Gamma(U,\mathcal A|_U)=(\mathcal A|_U)(U)=\mathcal A(U)$ and $(\pi|_U)_U=\pi_U$ by the definition of the restricted module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits].

source.place: Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 496) (2), H^p(U,F) = H^p(U,F|_U), used to pass from the derived functors of Gamma(U,-) on Mod(O_X) in 01EV to cohomology of the scheme U

proof.text: **Step 8 (cohomology of $U$ as derived functors).** The open subscheme $U$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $H^n(U,-)=R^nv$ ($n\ge0$) are the right derived functors of the global sections functor $v=\Gamma(U,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\textit{Ab}$, $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A(U)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]; this makes sense because $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is an abelian category with enough injectives [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] (applied to the scheme $U$), and $v$ is additive and left exact, since kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. (Whether $v$ takes values in abelian groups or in $\mathcal O_U(U)$-modules does not change the underlying groups $R^nv(\mathcal A)$, hence not their vanishing.)

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, second paragraph ("Next, we look at the long exact cohomology sequence ... for any open U subset X")

proof.text: **Step 9 (dimension shifting).** Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and apply the long exact sequence of the right derived functors $H^n(U,-)=R^nv$ of Step 8 [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal I|_U\to\mathcal Q|_U\to0$ of Step 7; since $\mathcal I|_U$ is injective in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ (Step 7), $H^n(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] (Stacks 015B). Case $p=1$: the piece $H^0(U,\mathcal I|_U)\to H^0(U,\mathcal Q|_U)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G|_U)\to H^1(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ is exact, and under the natural isomorphism $R^0v\cong v$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] its first map is $v(\pi|_U)=\pi_U:\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ (Step 7), which is surjective by Step 4 with $W=U$; hence $H^1(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$. This holds for every Cech-acyclic $\mathcal G$ and every open $U$, which is $P(1)$. Case $p\ge2$, assuming $P(p-1)$: the piece $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q|_U)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)\to H^p(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ is exact, and $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q|_U)=0$ by $P(p-1)$ applied to $\mathcal Q$, which is Cech-acyclic by Step 6; hence $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$, which is $P(p)$. By induction $P(p)$ holds for all $p\ge1$; with $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ (Step 1) this is the lemma.

source.place: Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish), proof, second paragraph ("Since I is injective we have H^n(U,I) = 0 for n > 0 (Derived Categories Lemma 015B). By the above we see that H^0(U,I) -> H^0(U,Q) is surjective and hence H^1(U,F) = 0 ... also H^1(U,Q) = 0 ... H^2(U,F) = 0. And so on and so forth.")
